request.state: Incident report 2026-09-12. At 02:14 UTC the payments gateway began returning HTTP 502 for roughly 30% of card authorisations in the EU region. The on-call engineer paged the database team at 02:20 after noticing connection pool exhaustion on the primary. A configuration change deployed at 01:58 had reduced the pool size from 200 to 20 as part of a cost-saving experiment that was meant to target the staging environment only. The change was rolled back at 02:41 and error rates returned to baseline by 02:47. During the incident, 1,842 customers saw failed payments; 311 of them retried successfully, and the remainder were sent an apology email with a retry link. No data was lost. Follow-up actions: add an environment guard to the deployment pipeline, alert on pool saturation above 80%, and review the experiment approval process. The customer support queue received 96 tickets referencing the outage, most asking whether they had been double charged. None were. Finance confirmed no duplicate settlements occurred. The postmortem was attended by payments, database, SRE and support leads, and the action items were assigned owners with due dates within two weeks. A separate, unrelated alert fired at 03:05 for disk usage on a logging node and was resolved by rotating logs. The incident severity was set to SEV-2 because customer impact was partial and time-limited.
